solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Greek character assesses joint for Jack Sparrow's vessel, say

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
to rate something is to assess or value it
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: Someone sizing up a hinge or joint for the ship in Pirates of the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' sounds like a person from Greece, but it means a letter of their alphabet. 'Say' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Jack Sparrow of the Pirates of the Caribbean films sails the Black Pearl, one example of a buccaneer's craft.

clue.text: Prelude of some quaint romances

indicators.note: 'some of' a phrase is only part of it, so the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: The opening chapter of some old-fashioned love stories.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the two words: quaINT ROmances.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name the opening section that comes before the main part of a piece of music or writing.

clue.text: Disciple's letters covered in beer

indicators.note: something covered in a substance is wrapped by it, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
letters delivered to you are your post, the British word for mail

explanation.surface: A follower's correspondence has been soaked by spilled beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay. Post is the British word for mail, which Americans may not reach for.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelve apostles were the chosen followers of Jesus, so an apostle is a disciple.

clue.text: Losing head, touch slippery fish

indicators.note: to lose the head is to drop the first letter of a word

parts.note: to touch something is to feel it

explanation.surface: A fish so slippery that touching it makes you lose your head.
explanation.walkthrough: FEEL without its first letter F leaves EEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long snakelike fish famous for their slimy skin that is hard to grip.

clue.text: Muscular companion of Nemo is perfectly fine

parts.note: a hunky person is big and muscular
Dory is the forgetful blue fish who helps search for Nemo in Finding Nemo

explanation.surface: A strong sidekick of Captain Nemo is in perfectly good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: Nemo suggests Jules Verne's submarine captain, but the companion is from the Pixar film Finding Nemo.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase describes a situation where everything is going well and nothing is wrong.

clue.text: Factory put underground?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an industrial site where things are manufactured
second meaning: to set a seed or bulb into the soil

explanation.surface: A factory being built below ground level.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that 'put underground' is not about a buried factory but about gardening.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for an industrial works and a verb for setting seeds into soil.

clue.text: Surrey's opener doesn't have trousers!

indicators.note: an opener comes first, so only the initial letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the county name
to lack something is not to have it

explanation.surface: A Surrey opening batsman has turned up to the cricket without his trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is an English county with a famous cricket club, and an opener is the batsman who goes in first, which makes the surface feel like sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Slacks are casual trousers, a common everyday synonym for loose-fitting legwear.

clue.text: Wander street, then go round and round

parts.note: St is the standard abbreviation for street
to roll is to turn over and over

explanation.surface: Someone ambles down the road and then starts spinning in circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Then' simply places one piece after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To stroll is to walk slowly and aimlessly, the same leisurely movement as to wander.

clue.text: Piece of yarn earl yanked, just about

indicators.note: a piece is only a part, so the letters come from within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters span the three words

explanation.surface: A nobleman tugs at a strand of wool until it has almost come loose.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across yarN EARL Yanked.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions mean almost, very close to but not quite completely.

clue.text: Writer's project regularly displayed

indicators.note: showing something at regular intervals means every other letter is kept

parts.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: An author's work is put on display at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking letters 1, 3, 5 and 7 of PrOjEcT gives P, O, E, T.
explanation.definitionFit: A poet is someone who composes verse, a particular kind of literary author.

clue.text: With great delight, attach video game controller

parts.note: joy is great delight
to stick something on is to attach it

explanation.surface: A gamer happily plugs in the controller for their console.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With great delight' reads as describing how the attaching is done, but it supplies the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A joystick is the lever-style handset used to steer and play on computers and consoles.

clue.text: High winds disrupted street jam

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gales have broken up a traffic jam in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Street jam' looks like a traffic hold-up, but its letters are the raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: The jet stream is a fast, narrow band of air current flowing high in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Right, leave the plane quickly, loser!

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
a pilot ejects to escape the aircraft in an emergency

explanation.surface: Someone shouts at a failure to bail out of the aircraft at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like an exclamation of agreement but is just the letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: A reject, as a noun, is a person or thing turned down as not good enough, close to a failure.

clue.text: Develop gun with no edges

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its outermost letters, so both ends are removed

parts.note: a revolver is a handgun

explanation.surface: An engineer designs a firearm with smoothed-off edges.
explanation.walkthrough: REVOLVER loses its first and last R to leave EVOLVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To evolve is to grow gradually into a more advanced form, as to develop does.

clue.text: So tube is moving slow?

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift out of place into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that the London Underground train is crawling along.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's Underground railway, which makes 'slow' read as a train's speed rather than a dim mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse describes someone slow to understand, the mental sense of slow rather than the speed sense.

clue.text: Quit ale, weirdly, and drink this instead?

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer to the noun: the drink you would have instead of ale

indicators.note: doing something weirdly means doing it in a strange, disordered fashion, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to give up beer and switch to something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful pointer: the answer is what you would be drinking in place of the ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Tequila is a Mexican spirit distilled from agave, an alternative alcoholic beverage to beer.

clue.text: Genuinely divine outside cosy home

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: holy means divine or sacred
a nest is a snug home, as for a bird

explanation.surface: Someone truly delighted, standing outside a snug little house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like the casual word for lovely, but here it means sacred.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adverbs mean truly or sincerely, without pretence or deceit.

clue.text: Wear armour regularly? That would be a mistake

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter is kept

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Should you put on a suit of armour every day? That would be unwise.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of wEaR aRmOuR spell E, R, R, O, R.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is something done wrong, the plain synonym for a slip or blunder.

clue.text: Starts to question unusual inventor patenting joke

indicators.note: the start of each word is its first letter, so only initials are kept

parts.note: the initial letters of four words

explanation.surface: People begin to doubt an eccentric inventor who is patenting a gag.
explanation.walkthrough: Initials of Question Unusual Inventor Patenting.
explanation.definitionFit: A quip is a witty remark, a short spoken jest.

clue.text: I give out cards? That's just perfect

parts.note: taken as written
to deal is to hand out the cards in a card game

explanation.surface: A player volunteers to be dealer and someone replies that this is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is taken literally as the letter, then the card-game verb follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal describes something as good as it could possibly be, with no flaws.

clue.text: Declares leader of Ecuador is disinclined

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of the country's name

explanation.surface: A report that Ecuador's president has announced he is reluctant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of Ecuador' suggests a president, but it is just the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be averse to something is to dislike it and be unwilling, the same as reluctant.

clue.text: Young lady's assistance accepted by some guys

indicators.note: what is accepted is taken in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: guys are men
aid is help or assistance

explanation.surface: A girl offers help and a group of fellows take her up on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'; AID goes inside MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Maiden is an old-fashioned literary word for a girl or unmarried woman.

clue.text: Spoil horse with no tail

indicators.note: a tail is the end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A horse whose tail has been cut off has been ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: MARE loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to damage or blemish it, so it is spoilt.

clue.text: Make barrel in an unusual way? Extraordinary

indicators.note: doing something unusually means not in the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cooper builds a cask by some strange method, and someone marvels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make barrel' reads as a craft instruction, but the two words supply all ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe something unusual enough to be worth comment or surprise.
